title: Jalebi: Crisp Fermented Batter Spirals in Saffron Syrup
summary: A lightly soured batter piped into spirals, fried crisp and dipped briefly in a saffron and cardamom syrup.
equipment: wide deep frying pan or karahi
piping bag with a 5 mm plain nozzle or a squeeze bottle

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk the plain flour, gram flour, cardamom and saffron together in the bowl. Whisk in the yoghurt, lukewarm water and food colouring if using until smooth, thick and falling from the whisk in a ribbon.

steps.title: Ferment overnight
steps.text: Cover the bowl and leave it somewhere warm for 12-24 h. It is ready when the top is dotted with bubbles and it smells pleasantly sour; the fermentation gives jalebi their tang and crisp, airy texture. Whisk briefly before using.

steps.title: Make the syrup
steps.text: Bring the sugar, 230 ml water, saffron, cardamom and lime juice to the boil, then simmer until it reaches 107-110 °C and feels slightly tacky between two fingers. Add the rose water if using and let it cool to 65-70 °C, then hold it there. Syrup that is too hot softens the jalebi; too cool and it will not soak in.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into the wide pan to about 2.5 cm deep and heat to 165 °C. A shallow layer at a moderate heat lets the spirals cook through and crisp before they brown.

steps.title: Pipe the spirals
steps.text: Fill the piping bag and pipe 7-8 cm spirals directly into the oil, 3 or 4 at a time, working from the outside and finishing in the centre. Keep the bag moving steadily so the ropes stay even.

steps.title: Fry until crisp
steps.text: Fry for 45-60 s on each side, turning once with tongs, until crisp and lightly golden. Keep checking that the oil stays at 165 °C between batches.

steps.title: Soak and serve
steps.text: Lift each jalebi out, shake off the oil and drop it into the warm syrup for 30 s, pressing gently so it fills the hollow ropes. Set on the rack and repeat with the rest; serve warm or at room temperature the same day.

tips: A common mistake is batter that is too thin: it spreads into blobs. It should flow in a steady, thick rope.
If the kitchen is cool, ferment the batter in the oven with only the light on.
Fry one test spiral first to check the oil temperature and the batter thickness.
Keep the syrup warm on the lowest heat and check it with the thermometer.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Jalebi are best eaten the day they are made. Keep leftovers loosely covered at room temperature for up to 1 day; they soften as they stand.
